threads.name: I Would Prefer Not To
threads.why: A 170-year line of people who simply stop cooperating, first as fiction, then as an argument about work.

threads.name: The Eternal Return
threads.why: Nietzsche's thought experiment (would you live this exact life again, forever?) keeps getting turned into novels, and it ends up back at Vonnegut.

threads.name: The Author Walks In
threads.why: The comic novel that knows it is a novel, from Cervantes to the moment Vonnegut sits down at the bar in Midland City.

threads.name: Books Made of Books
threads.why: The library as labyrinth, trap and fire: novels built out of imaginary books, commentaries and archives.

threads.name: Out of Gogol's Overcoat
threads.why: A teacher-and-student line from Gogol's clerk to the Iowa workshop where Vonnegut taught John Irving.

threads.name: From Dresden to Copenhagen
threads.why: The air war Billy Pilgrim survived, and the physicists whose work finished it, ending on a question about what Heisenberg knew.

threads.name: Pranks as Politics
threads.why: Discordians, Situationists and chaos magicians all decided the joke was the revolution; the line runs through my Robert Anton Wilson shelf.

threads.name: What Is It Like to Be
threads.why: From a tick's world to an alien ocean: the question of other minds, asked of animals, plants and finally something no science can enter.

threads.name: Job's Question
threads.why: Why do the innocent suffer? Asked in scripture, answered with a wager, a knife, a returned ticket, a starship, and finally a joke.

threads.name: The Detective Sentence
threads.why: Crime fiction as a style lab: from Hammett's bare lines to Pynchon's stoned haze, the lean-to-maximal axis in one genre.

threads.name: Writing Back
threads.why: Four classics, each answered decades later by someone the original left voiceless. Read them in pairs.

threads.name: Is This the Simulation?
threads.why: One question, 2,300 years old: how would I know if this world were staged? Each answer gets more literal.

threads.name: Rules That Make Worlds
threads.why: Simple rules produce endless complexity, in cellular automata and in the Oulipo's constrained novels. The same idea in math and in style.

threads.name: The Haiku Goes West
threads.why: How seventeen Japanese syllables became American poetry: Bashō to Pound to Williams to the Beats, and back to Zen.

threads.name: Kafka Creates His Precursors
threads.why: Borges argued that every writer creates his own precursors: after Kafka you can see him in Zeno, Kierkegaard and Melville. This thread tests the idea.

threads.name: Plato's cave, six rooms
threads.why: The same allegory filmed six ways, from an Italian art film to a kung fu blockbuster. Somebody wakes up and finds the walls were painted.

threads.name: The siege
threads.why: A small group, one building, the night outside full of enemies. I keep loving this shape without noticing it is the same film.

threads.name: Samurai and gunslingers trade hats
threads.why: Japan borrowed the western, Italy stole it back, and then Japan and Korea took it again. A forty-year game of telephone.

threads.name: The professional, stripped
threads.why: Men who do one job with their hands and say almost nothing. Bresson's prison films turn into the most stylish crime films I know.

threads.name: God's lonely man
threads.why: A man alone in a room, writing in a journal, waiting for grace or a gun. Paul Schrader spent fifty years remaking one Bresson film, and the trail runs straight through my Scorsese.

threads.name: Two men in a car, the long way
threads.why: The buddy movie before it became a formula, and after. Midnight Run (already seen, not on the list) is the hinge this whole thread swings on.

threads.name: Lovers on the run
threads.why: Two kids, a car, a gun, and the law a few miles behind. Godard's homage to American B movies boomerangs back into Tarantino's scripts by way of Senegal.

threads.name: The screen talks back
threads.why: Seventy years of films that saw what television would do to us, ending with a man who finds out he's the show.

threads.name: The film that nearly killed its makers
threads.why: Jungle shoots, river madness, and the documentaries filmed beside the disasters. The making-of is often as good as the movie.

threads.name: Holy fools
threads.why: The innocent who walks through the world and exposes everyone around him. Chaplin to Dostoevsky to a donkey to a Washington garden.

threads.name: Counting the last days
threads.why: Someone learns the time is short and has to decide what the life was. Tolstoy's Ivan Ilyich keeps getting reborn in another city.

threads.name: Is that really them?
threads.why: Real people playing themselves, reenacting their own lives, or lying about them on camera. Welles started it as a joke and it became a whole cinema.

threads.name: The fake band
threads.why: Bands that were invented, played by actors, or so real they look like parody. The rock film as a hall of mirrors.

threads.name: Bird's cymbal
threads.why: One story, Jo Jones throwing a cymbal at a teenage Charlie Parker, travels from a jazz biopic into the best film about obsession I know. Then it walks back through 1988, the year of three jazz films, and ends somewhere happier.

threads.name: The house on the hill
threads.why: Kurosawa put a rich man's house above a slum. Korean cinema built a whole new wave on that view, and on the 1980s it came out of.

threads.name: In tempore belli
threads.why: Six composers answer the same war, and a string quartet that formed because of one of these pieces carries it to the end.

threads.name: Jonny Greenwood's teachers
threads.why: How the strings and the strange keyboard on Kid A came from two classical scores, and then went back into the concert hall.

threads.name: In a Silent Way, scattered
threads.why: Everyone in the room on one Miles session went off and started their own band; follow the sidemen and you get the whole fusion decade, ending at Mingus.

threads.name: Duke's bass line
threads.why: Mingus learned the bass from Ellington's band, got fired by Ellington, wrote him love letters, and then recorded with him; Miles closes it with an elegy.

threads.name: Marc Ribot's busted guitar
threads.why: One sideman's guitar sound, from Rain Dogs through downtown jazz and Cuban son to T Bone Burnett's Americana and back to Waits.

threads.name: Faust, Woyzeck and the devil's cabaret
threads.why: Two old stories, the deal with the devil and the poor soldier Woyzeck, run from Stravinsky and Berg through Weill to Tom Waits and back to the cabaret.

threads.name: Jack White's record collection
threads.why: The White Stripes as a reading list: the blues and garage records he learned from, then the old singers he went back and produced.

threads.name: From the Kitchen to the dance floor
threads.why: Arthur Russell played cello behind Ginsberg and made disco records in the same years; follow him and you reach the room LCD Soundsystem came out of.

threads.name: Manfred Eicher's cathedral
threads.why: One label, ECM, puts a medieval vocal group, a Norwegian saxophonist, Keith Jarrett and Arvo Pärt in the same reverb.

threads.name: Bach, rewired
threads.why: One composer passed through a Soviet piano cycle, a Brazilian song, a Moog synthesizer and a NASA record; Glenn Gould is at both ends.

threads.name: Dark Was the Night
threads.why: One Blind Willie Johnson recording leaves the planet, scores a Wenders film, and through Ry Cooder leads to Mali, Havana and the Sahara.

threads.name: Ron Carter's bass to Thundercat's
threads.why: Miles's second quintet shows up on a Tribe record, and the line runs through Dilla and Flying Lotus to the LA jazz revival.

threads.name: Kool Keith to Tom Waits
threads.why: The weird wing of hip-hop passes producer to producer until it ends on an indie record with Tom Waits singing through a megaphone.

threads.name: No Depression
threads.why: One Carter Family song named a whole movement; follow it from the high lonesome to Son Volt, O Brother and Billy Strings.

threads.name: What Illinois is made of
threads.why: Illinois sounds like Guaraldi plus Reich plus a church band; follow those parts, then the people Sufjan made records with.
